questions.knowledge_point: Rearranging and Solving a Quadratic Equation With Complex Roots
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation in standard form by bringing all of the terms to the left-hand side. This gives the equation

$$
{x}^{2}+2x+5=0.
$$

We can find the roots of a quadratic equation using the quadratic formula:

$$
x=\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a}
$$

In this case, the coefficients are $a=1,\,b=2,$ and $c=5.$ Substituting these values into the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{{2}^{2}-4(1)(5)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{4-20}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{-16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm 4\,\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-1\pm 2\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=-1+2\,\text{i}$ and $x=-1-2\,\text{i}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Quadratic Equation With Complex Roots by Completing the Square
questions.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}+16x+164=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
questions.worked_solution:
We first move the constant to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+16x+164 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+16x & =-164\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+16x & =-164 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 8x+{8}^{2}-{8}^{2} & =-164 \\ (x+8)^{2}-64 & =-164 \\ (x+8)^{2} & =-100\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=8,\,q=-100,$ and $p+q=-92.$

We now solve the equation using the square root method.

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+8)^{2} & =-100 \\ x+8 & =\pm \sqrt{-100} \\ x+8 & =\pm 10\,\text{i} \\ x & =-8\pm 10\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=-8+10\,\text{i}$ and $x=-8-10\,\text{i}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Quadratic Equation With Complex Roots by Completing the Square
questions.problem: What are the solutions of the equation $(x-2)^{2}=-49?$
questions.worked_solution:
The left-hand side is a perfect square. Therefore, we can solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =-49 \\ x-2 & =\pm \sqrt{-49} \\ x-2 & =\pm 7\,\text{i} \\ x & =2\pm 7\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=2+7\,\text{i}$ and $x=2-7\,\text{i}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Quadratic Equation With Complex Roots by Completing the Square
questions.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}-6x+34=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
questions.worked_solution:
We first move the constant to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-6x+34 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-6x & =-34\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-6x & =-34 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 3x+{3}^{2}-{3}^{2} & =-34 \\ (x-3)^{2}-9 & =-34 \\ (x-3)^{2} & =-25\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-3,\,q=-25,$ and $p+q=-28.$

Finally, we solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =-25 \\ x-3 & =\pm \sqrt{-25} \\ x-3 & =\pm 5\,\text{i} \\ x & =3\pm 5\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=3+5\,\text{i}$ and $x=3-5\,\text{i}.$
